description:
## Empirical anchor

Arc 42 validate-spec first-run (2026-05-18, substrate SHA 8a49282, artifact at agents/observation/spec-validation/mechanical-check-results.md):
- **check-1 §-ref resolution**: 144/274 §-refs FAIL to resolve (parser WP-1 limitation realized as anticipated at design time + accepted by ARGUS rev1)
- **check-2 ticket-status (partial)**: 36 STRANGE classifications from ambiguous-claim-prose parser failure (in addition to 6 genuine claim-vs-actual mismatches which are routine POLYBIUS fix-now)

Root cause per ADA's Arc 42 ground-check finding #4 + DAEDALUS's design WP-1: the bare-`§N.X` resolver over-matches the spec's own section headings (e.g., a spec body reference to `§13.11 Pass 9` resolves to multiple places where §13.11 appears: the section heading itself AND any narrative prose citing §13.11). The check-1 resolver currently counts ALL matches as PASS-ambiguous OR FAIL; correct behavior would skip refs that ARE the spec's own headings + count only actual cross-reference resolutions.

Same parser-class limitation affects check-2's STRANGE classification: when validate-spec tries to parse claim-prose like "stoa--X (P3) — `[scope-description]`" to extract claimed-status, parser hits ambiguous prose patterns and routes to STRANGE rather than auto-classifying.

## Fix shape

Two-part refinement:

**Part 1 (check-1 §-ref resolver)**: implement heuristic "skip refs that ARE spec's own headings":
- Build set of spec's own section headings from `^## §N|^### §N|^#### §N` pattern
- For each ref like `§13.11`, check if `§13.11` IS itself a heading in the set
- If yes: skip (it's a self-reference within the section, not a cross-ref); count only OTHER citations of `§13.11` from outside the §13.11 section
- If no: proceed with existing resolution logic

**Part 2 (check-2 claim-prose parser)**: tighten claim-extraction heuristics OR pivot to structured-frontmatter approach:
- Option α: tighter regex on `bw show` output for claimed-status fields
- Option β: have validate-spec require frontmatter-style status annotations in §13.5-§13.9a candidate enumerations (e.g., `- **stoa--XXX (P3, status:closed)** — ...`)
- α is non-canonical-touching but probably won't get below ~10% STRANGE; β is canonical-touching but reduces STRANGE to near-zero

DAEDALUS picks α / β / hybrid at design time.

## Sequencing

P3. Arc 43+. After Pass 10 stellation behavioral validation OR if stellation surfaces parser-limitation blocking Pass 10 readiness, prioritize.

## Cross-references

- Arc 42 ship (PR # to-be-filled at ship): validate-spec build-then-use + first-run results documented in mech-check-results.md
- Arc 42 design.md §6 WP-1 (DAEDALUS self-flagged parser limitation at design time)
- Arc 42 ARGUS rev1 acceptance (parser refinement = future-arc work, not Arc 42 blocker)
- Arc 42 A20 motivated-reasoning property held: validate-spec produced honest FAILs vs auto-PASS
- stoa--bbi — refined-principle thesis evidence (parser limitation IS the operationally-acceptable residue per "structural fixes narrow drift surface but require iteration to close")
- Companion findings: ADA Arc 42 surface #1 (P15/P16 awk-bracket drift) + #2 (P25 grep quote-style) = mn3-class probe-drift candidates for same future refinement bundle

## Out of scope

- Replacing the validate-spec skill architecture (Arc 42 ship is canonical)
- Extending validate-spec to non-spec-met checks
- Building a separate inspection-agent skill for parser-strangeness triage (per Arc 42 A8 ε inline-triage decision; revisit only if strangeness-frequency justifies separate skill)
title: Refine validate-spec parsers — check-1 §-ref resolver heading-skip heuristic + check-2 claim-status disambiguation (Arc 42 first-run WP-1 residue)
